I have loaded and analyzed the uploaded file `T077_ref.csv` (assumed to be the "ghost.csv" mentioned in the request as it is the only available data file).

### Spectral Analysis
The spectrum consists of a Raman shift axis from 200 to 2000 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ and corresponding intensity values. I performed peak detection using a height threshold of 50, which identified several distinct vibrational modes.

**Detected Peaks:**
- **$1001\text{ cm}^{-1}$**: Intensity 1000.00 (Primary peak)
- **$1602\text{ cm}^{-1}$**: Intensity 629.68
- **$1031\text{ cm}^{-1}$**: Intensity 427.83
- **$1450\text{ cm}^{-1}$**: Intensity 219.54
- **$620\text{ cm}^{-1}$**: Intensity 179.17
- **$1155\text{ cm}^{-1}$**: Intensity 143.11
- **$1183\text{ cm}^{-1}$**: Intensity 124.34
- **$795\text{ cm}^{-1}$**: Intensity 99.91

### Interpretation and Conclusion
The spectral signature is highly characteristic of **Polystyrene**. The dominant peak at $\sim 1001\text{ cm}^{-1}$ corresponds to the symmetric ring breathing mode of the phenyl group, while the peaks at $1602\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (C=C stretching) and $1450\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (CH$_2$ bending/ring vibrations) are classic markers for this polymer. The presence and relative intensities of these modes provide a high-confidence identification.
